One picture of where everything sits, then the three paths a request can take. Every scenario
follows one of those paths, so the table at the end names the path for each, and each scenario's
page says what happens along it. **Solid** parts are built and running; **dashed** parts are
planned, labelled with the phase that brings them. [The plan](design/plan.md) holds the reasons.

## Where everything sits

```{mermaid}
flowchart TB
  classDef planned stroke-dasharray: 5 5

  subgraph mac["heartsbane · the Mac"]
    direction LR
    orca["Orca"]
    claude_mac["Claude Code,<br/>Claude Desktop"]
    pi_mac["pi"]
    webapp["web UI,<br/>Safari web app"]
    term["terminal"]
  end

  subgraph phone["Android phone"]
    pwa["web UI,<br/>home-screen app"]
  end

  anthropic(("Anthropic"))
  apps["my pipelines and<br/>homelab apps · Phase 3"]:::planned

  subgraph spark["brightroar · the Spark"]
    tss["tailscale serve,<br/>HTTPS 443"]
    owui["Open WebUI · 127.0.0.1:3000<br/>root's Compose"]
    searx["SearXNG · 127.0.0.1:8888<br/>root's Compose"]
    agent_tmux["pi and Claude Code<br/>as agent, in tmux"]
    litellm["LiteLLM, a key per app<br/>Phase 3"]:::planned
    swap["llama-swap · 127.0.0.1:9100<br/>as spark, keys"]
    gate["spark-gate<br/>Phase 2"]:::planned
    brake["memory brake<br/>as spark"]
    engines["engines · 127.0.0.1:5800 and up<br/>Gemma, embeddings, whisper, coder"]
    vllm["vLLM, only if a coder needs it<br/>Phase 5"]:::planned
  end

  subgraph nas["Synology"]
    ntfy["ntfy and the watchdog<br/>Phase 2"]:::planned
    shares["shares and backups<br/>Phase 4"]:::planned
  end

  orca -- starts --> claude_mac
  orca -- starts --> pi_mac
  claude_mac --> anthropic
  webapp -- "HTTPS over Tailscale" --> tss
  pwa -- "HTTPS over Tailscale" --> tss
  pi_mac -- "SSH tunnel, make tunnel" --> swap
  term -- "ssh brightroar-agent" --> agent_tmux
  tss --> owui
  owui --> searx
  owui --> swap
  agent_tmux --> swap
  agent_tmux -- "its Claude Code" --> anthropic
  apps -.-> litellm
  litellm -.-> swap
  swap -- "spark launch" --> engines
  swap -.-> vllm
  brake -- "unloads through llama-swap" --> engines
  gate -.-> engines
  gate -.-> ntfy
  agent_tmux -.-> shares
```

- **Everything on the Spark listens on 127.0.0.1**, except SSH and `tailscale serve`'s port 443.
  The tailnet's rules let my own devices reach the Spark on those two ports only, and ufw allows
  SSH alone from the LAN.
- **Three accounts on the Spark.** Mine, the admin; `spark`, which runs llama-swap, the engines and
  the brake; and `agent`, for coding agents in tmux, with no sudo, no docker and keys of its own.
  Root runs the web services from its own copies of their units.
- **Claude never uses the Spark's models.** Claude Code and Claude Desktop talk straight to
  Anthropic, wherever they run; Orca only starts them. The Spark is a separate mode.

## Reaching the Spark

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  classDef planned stroke-dasharray: 5 5

  piT["pi on the Mac<br/>in a terminal or Orca"]
  ui["web UI<br/>on the Mac or the phone"]
  piA["pi as agent<br/>in tmux on the Spark"]
  cc["Claude Code<br/>anywhere"]
  app["an app with its own key<br/>Phase 3"]:::planned

  tunnel["SSH tunnel<br/>over Tailscale, or the LAN alias"]
  serve["tailscale serve, 443<br/>Tailscale only"]
  owui["Open WebUI"]
  searx["SearXNG"]
  swap["llama-swap, 127.0.0.1:9100<br/>a key on every request"]
  litellm["LiteLLM on a LAN port<br/>Phase 3"]:::planned
  anthropic(("Anthropic"))

  piT --> tunnel --> swap
  ui --> serve --> owui --> swap
  owui --> searx
  piA --> swap
  cc --> anthropic
  app -.-> litellm -.-> swap
```

pi on the Mac reaches llama-swap only while `make tunnel` runs, since nothing on the Spark listens
beyond 127.0.0.1 but SSH. The web UI needs Tailscale: on another tailnet, over WireGuard, the LAN
alias still carries SSH and so pi's tunnel, but the web UI waits. `agent`'s pi needs no tunnel. From
Phase 3, apps reach the models through LiteLLM, each with a key of its own.

## Loading a model

```{mermaid}
flowchart TD
  classDef planned stroke-dasharray: 5 5

  req["a request names a model"] --> loaded{"already loaded?"}
  loaded -- yes --> answer["the engine answers"]
  loaded -- no --> launch["llama-swap starts it<br/>through spark launch"]
  launch --> held{"is the brake holding<br/>new loads?"}
  held -- yes --> refuse["refused, with its reason<br/>make status shows it"]
  held -- no --> fits{"does its footprint fit in<br/>free memory, less the reserve?"}
  fits -- no --> refuse
  fits -- yes --> load["the engine loads"] --> answer
  low["free memory falls<br/>toward the freeze band"] --> brake["the brake warns, then holds new loads<br/>and unloads models, on-demand ones first"]
  brake --> held
  gate["Phase 2, the gate: a live fit check, one load at a time,<br/>idle unload, session pins, make-room, notifications"]:::planned
  gate -.-> launch
```

A model loads only if it fits: nothing is evicted to make room, and nothing is swapped for a
smaller model. Free memory is the smaller of `MemAvailable` and what the GPU can allocate, and the
reserve stays free, because overcommitting a GB10 can freeze it without an out-of-memory kill.

## Apps and speech (Phase 3, planned)

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  classDef planned stroke-dasharray: 5 5

  app["an app or pipeline<br/>with its own key"]:::planned --> litellm["LiteLLM: limits and a wait per key,<br/>refusals inline, the real model named"]:::planned
  litellm -.-> pg[("Postgres<br/>keys and usage")]:::planned
  litellm -.-> swap["llama-swap"]
  swap --> chat["chat and embeddings"]
  swap --> stt["whisper, interactive"]
  swap -.-> batch["whisper, batch"]:::planned
  swap -.-> diar["speaker labels"]:::planned
```

Today the web UI and pi reach llama-swap directly with llama-swap's own keys. From Phase 3, my
own pipelines and homelab apps come in through LiteLLM instead, each with a key of its own; it
never logs what they send.

## When something breaks, and upkeep

These follow runbooks rather than a request path: a freeze while I'm away
([S13](scenarios/s13-freeze-away.md)), the NAS down ([S15](scenarios/s15-nas-down.md)), a rebuild
after a factory reset ([S18](scenarios/s18-rebuild.md)), and upgrade day
([S23](scenarios/s23-upgrade-day.md); [Updates](how-to/updates.md)).
